### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/page.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via RecordRelatedListProps (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via RecordRelatedListProps (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via RecordRelatedListProps (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/page.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c6139f264ca28eed09717e7b0396f2a69aea9bb2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1b8a893ecd86df7d2ae5b6cf516cd7182c98dba0` — the merge of head `d4b3e7264f0430a07cde9e6c7719b904db46a904` into base `c6139f264ca28eed09717e7b0396f2a69aea9bb2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1b8a893ecd86df7d2ae5b6cf516cd7182c98dba0 && git checkout 1b8a893ecd86df7d2ae5b6cf516cd7182c98dba0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c6139f264ca28eed09717e7b0396f2a69aea9bb2 d4b3e7264f0430a07cde9e6c7719b904db46a904 && git checkout -B drift-repro c6139f264ca28eed09717e7b0396f2a69aea9bb2 && git merge --no-ff d4b3e7264f0430a07cde9e6c7719b904db46a904

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c6139f264ca28eed09717e7b0396f2a69aea9bb2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c6139f264ca28eed09717e7b0396f2a69aea9bb2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d4b3e7264f0430a07cde9e6c7719b904db46a904`
Local-runs: none

Read for this record: card #23134 (body and both comments), ruling comment 6137226306 on objectstack-ai/objectui#12296, PR #23205 (body, file list, net diff: 6 files, +316 / -2), the head's check-runs, `origin/main` of this repo at `107853ced` and of objectui at `cea429b98` for context. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The one key, on the one block — right.** `ComponentPropsMap['record:related_list']` (`RecordRelatedListProps`, `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`) gains `parentDataSource: ElementDataSourceSchema.optional()`. That is the ruling's whole order on this repo: one parent-record binding key on `record:related_list`, and nothing else became authorable. `PageComponentSchema`, `ElementDataSourceSchema` and `page.zod.ts` are not in the diff; the node-level `dataSource` is byte-identical; `packages/lint` is untouched, so no new `validate` finding rode in (the ruling's own ⛔).
- **The props door, not a node key — right, and the card's `page.zod.ts` path was correctly not followed.** `PageComponentSchema` is one shape for every component type, so a key there would be authorable on all of them; `ComponentPropsMap` is the per-type door. Pinned (test file, group C): every other row refuses `parentDataSource` by `unrecognized_keys`, and the two retired rows (`ai:chat_window`, `user:profile`) refuse the whole bag. The dispatch claim already named this relocation.
- **The shape, by reference — right.** `ElementDataSourceSchema` (`page.zod.ts:244` on `origin/main`) is the lazy `strictObject` `{ object, view?, filter?, sort?, limit? }` with no defaults and alias spellings refused with guidance; the key's inner def is pinned identical to it and to the object arm of `PageComponentSchema.dataSource` (test group A), so there is one declaration and no copy to drift. The API arm (`ElementApiDataSourceSchema`) is not admitted: the card fixes the shape as (object, view, filter, sort, limit) and objectui's strict face for the three sibling record blocks takes the object binding alone (`RECORD_BLOCK_DATA_SOURCE = stripImportedDefaults(SpecElementDataSourceSchema)`, `packages/types/src/zod/public-blocks.zod.ts:666`). The new import is cycle-free: `page.zod.ts` imports from `./view.zod` and `../shared/*` only, nothing from `./component.zod`. Refusals at the key's own path are pinned by code and path (group B).
- **The name `parentDataSource` — right.** Measured: the three sibling record blocks read their one binding as `schema.dataSource` (objectui `plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordBinding.tsx`, `isBound`), the one other block with a parent half, `record:line_items`, spells it `parentObject` / `parentId` (`component.zod.ts:2618-2620`), and neither repository carried `parentDataSource` before this PR (zero hits on both `origin/main`). The `dataSource` stem keeps the two bindings in one family and the `parent` prefix names which record; the six rejected spellings in the PR body are rejected for sound reasons (`parentRecord` reads as a value, `recordDataSource` does not say which, `parentSource` collides with the shape's own `source` alias).
- **The stated read rule — right, and it is the sibling rule as objectui actually implements it.** The describe says: the FIRST row of the bound set by its `sort` is the parent, `limit: 1` is how an author says one row is meant, no row is a loud absence and never an empty list, `relationshipValueField` is read on that row. `recordBinding.tsx`'s module doc at objectui `origin/main`: first row by the binding's `sort`, one row ever asked for, zero rows draws the record-not-found state, `objectui validate` warns on a record binding without `limit: 1`. The fallback is stated as the card orders: absent, the record page's record context remains the parent.
- **The describe text — right.** It carries the three facts the card names (this key is the parent record; the record context is the fallback when absent; `dataSource` on this block is the child rows and is never read as the parent). It opens with `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]`, the spelling the three existing planned describes use (`page.zod.ts:502`, `:932`; `view.zod.ts:1874`) and the one `check-liveness.mts` `MARKER_RE.planned` reads (`:499-504`). No author-facing string carries a tracker number: the `.describe()` string and the generated `component.mdx` row are clean; `#23134`, `#6953`, the objectui numbers and the ruling comment id sit only in the TSDoc block, as this file's existing TSDoc already does (`[#18639]`, `[#13855]`). The nested-shape table inherits the shared shape's own describes (`limit`: "Max records to display"), which is what by-reference means and what the ruling ordered.
- **The generated and recorded artifacts — right.** One authorable-surface row, `ui/RecordRelatedListProps:parentDataSource`; the shape's own `ui/ElementDataSource:*` rows already exist (`ui.json:444-448`), so by-reference adds no nested rows. `component.mdx` gains the key's row and the nested-shape table. The liveness record is one PLANNED RECORD sentence appended to the `liveness/page.json` `_note`, following the #23016 `ElementApiDataSourceSchema` sentence in the same `_note`, because the walk stops at the recorded undrilled `page/regions` container and no component-level key can hold a row. `Type Check · source gates` (the lane that runs `check:generated`, `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs`, `lint.yml:5017-5142`) and `Spec property liveness` are both green on this head.
- **The objectui side — a note, not a finding.** objectui's strict face builds the block's `properties` bag from `SpecRecordRelatedListProps` by import (`public-blocks.zod.ts:753-754`), so the key reaches objectui's door with the spec release and needs no re-declaration there; until then the pinned spec refuses it as unknown, which is what PLANNED means. The related-list leg of objectstack-ai/objectui#12294 is correctly not in this PR.
- **One wording note, not blocking.** The describe says the key takes "the shape `dataSource` takes"; since #23016 the node-level `dataSource` is a union (object binding or API binding) and this key takes the object arm only. The describe names the object binding explicitly in the same sentence, so it reads correctly as written; "the object binding `dataSource` takes" would be exact.
- **Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-13T08:53Z; conclusions are the gate verdicts.** 39 runs: 27 success, 5 skipped, 7 in progress, 0 failure. Green: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint · ESLint`, the other Lint lanes, `Build Docs`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the claim and single-writer guards. In progress, reported as such and not assumed: `Test Core (1/6)` through `(6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace`; their aggregates `Test Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` are therefore not yet present on this head. Skipped are the full-battery lanes (`Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance`, the dogfood shards, the opt-in tarball smoke). The landing waits for the two aggregates as it would for any PR; nothing in this record relieves that.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23134-related-list-parent-data-source.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, body carrying `Clause-②: yes (widening)` plus the key, the single-record rule, the fallback, the `dataSource`-unchanged sentence and the PLANNED sentence — every element the card's step 2 orders. The PR body's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` matches. `yes` takes at least `minor`, and the diff publishes exactly one optional additive key (the inferred `RecordRelatedListProps` type widens by one optional member; no export added, removed or renamed), so `minor` is the right level. Not `skip-changeset`: `@objectstack/spec` publishes. The `(#23134)` on the changeset title is this package's CHANGELOG convention (over two thousand such citations on `origin/main`). `Check Changeset` is green. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 — the fork clause and `page-field-unknown`: judged independently from `origin/main`, not a fork; the seat's reading A stands.** `packages/lint/src/validate-page-field-bindings.ts`'s related-list branch calls `checkRefs(split.parent, objectName, where)` under the comment "`relationshipValueField` names a field on the PARENT (page) object", where `objectName` is the walk's generic `strName(dataSource?.object) ?? strName(props?.object) ?? inheritedObject` (`page-walk.ts:136-137`), and `relatedListFieldRefs` (`:408-437`) resolves the child side from `properties.objectName` alone. So with the published child binding, the parent-side ref is checked against the CHILD object and the child-side refs against nothing. That is a resolution defect against the rule's own stated reading, not a reader that gives `dataSource` the parent meaning: the rule's comment, its interface docblock ("refs resolved against the PARENT object, the record the list hangs off"), and every other reader of the block hold the child meaning — objectui's renderer (parent from `useRecordContext()`), objectui's CLI binding-limit and related-list-binding tests, objectui's `public-blocks.zod.ts` ("its binding is the binding of its CHILD rows"), and this repo's other three lint readers with a `dataSource` read near this block (`validate-action-name-refs.ts`, which resolves the list's actions against `dataSource.object` as the RELATED object; `validate-component-props.ts`; `validate-preset-comparands.ts`). The fix is a resolution fix in `packages/lint` (parent-side refs against `parentDataSource.object` when present, else the page object) and is not this PR's; the dispatch brief says it is filed as #23207, which this review did not read, as it is not among its inputs. Not escalated.
- **Dev flag — the key lives in `component.zod.ts`, not the card's `page.zod.ts`:** answered above (props door); the dispatch claim already named the relocation. Not a deviation from the ruling.
- **Dev flag — liveness as a `_note` sentence with no row:** answered above; the precedent is in the same `_note`, and the liveness gate is green.
- **Dev flag — `check:platform-checklist` exits 1 locally:** its inputs on this branch are byte-identical to `origin/main` (the dev's `git diff` over the gate's input paths is empty, and the absent symbol has zero hits on `origin/main`), so it is a main-red under the lane's convention and not this diff's; `Lint & Repo Gates` on this head is green. Noted, no action here.
- **Dev deviations:** the model-free commit-trailer pair follows AGENTS.md, which outranks the harness reminder; the `-- --maxWorkers=2` flag was probably dropped by vitest, which leaves the run whole-package as intended; the `_note` form is answered above. None blocks.
- **Out-of-scope findings:** the `page:tabs` count probe reading the parent from `ctx.data.id` is the objectui leg's to feed (carrier objectstack-ai/objectui#12294); `objectName` still being required beside a child `dataSource` predates this card. Both correctly noted and not fixed here.
- **Governance:** no governed surface in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green); 318 changed lines; head repo is the base repo; the PR is draft with auto-merge unarmed, as a PR awaiting its contract review should be.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23134-related-list-parent-binding`
Reviewed-by: `session_01BRQ9Mp1yH7R1az6MaUM18H`

**VERDICT: PASS**
